In this lesson, you will construct a basic diode modulator and demodulator circuit.
INTRODUCTIONM
After constructing the circuits you will verify circuit operation by measuring signals.
The circuits you will construct are the basic diode modulator and demodulator circuits.
Because of their simplicity and proven reliability these circuits are found in many types of equipment.
The basic diode modulator circuit is used in most inexpensive CB radio transmitters.
The basic diode demodulator circuit is used in most AM and CB radio receivers.
Let's begin the lesson on BASIC AM CIRCUIT CONSTRUCTION...................

1. Connect CH1 to PC1 Pin E. Set the oscilloscope Time/Div control to 2 ms. This is the 1 kHz information signal from PC130-322. Notice that the waveform is a sine wave with no modulation or amplitude variations. variations.

2. Connect CH1 to PC1 Pin D. Set the oscilloscope Time/Div control to 0.2 ms. This is the 1 kHz modulating signal from the modulation section of the function generator. Notice that there is a small 100 kHz signal riding on the 1 kHz signal.

This is due to the 100 kHz carrier signal being fed back through R2 in this simple modulator circuit. Transistor modulators do not have this problem, however, normally the feedback does not present a problem in the circuit operation.

6. Leave the CH1 probe in place and reconnect L1 and C1. Set the Time/Div to 0.2 ms. Notice that you now have a complete AM waveform. The tank circuit developed the negative cycles.
